metadata.summary: Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.
metadata.content: Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on Uefa to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on Uefa to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem Monday 5 October 2026 08:40, UK Image: Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future. The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia. The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics , with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War. This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium. Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. metadata.content: Singapore GP 2026 Sprint weekend dates, schedule, weather, UK start time and how to watch or stream F1 race at Marina Bay Circuit live on Sky Sports | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Singapore GP 2026 Sprint weekend dates, schedule, weather, UK start time and how to watch or stream F1 race at Marina Bay Circuit live on Sky Sports Find out the race-week schedule, weather and how to watch the Sprint weekend at the Singapore Grand Prix; watch every session starting this Friday with Practice at 9.30am and Sprint Qualifying at 1.30pm, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Monday 5 October 2026 06:25, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Look back at some of the most dramatic moments to have taken place at the Singapore Grand Prix Formula 1 concludes its Asian triple-header with a Sprint weekend at the Singapore Grand Prix. A dramatic race in Malaysia last time out saw Max Verstappen secure Red Bull's first victory of the season, while Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the Drivers' Championship to 84 points over George Russell, who was forced to retire late on with a power unit issue. Lewis Hamilton produced an impressive recovery drive, charging from 18th to the podium after a strategy gamble failed to pay off in the mixed conditions. The Ferrari driver will be confident of another strong result at the next round in Singapore, where the tight, twisty streets are likely to suit his strengths.
